title: KS3 Computing — The CPU & Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle
subtitle: CPU architecture, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, and factors affecting CPU performance.

data.targetWord: Central Processing Unit; the main component of a computer that fetches, decodes, and executes all program instructions

examples.en-GB: The CPU executes billions of instructions per second to run the operating system and all applications.

data.targetWord: Arithmetic and Logic Unit; the component inside the CPU that performs all arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction) and logical comparisons (AND, OR, NOT)

examples.en-GB: When the program needs to add two numbers, the ALU performs the calculation and stores the result in the Accumulator.

data.targetWord: the component inside the CPU that manages and coordinates the fetch-decode-execute cycle, directing data flow between the CPU's sub-components and RAM without performing calculations itself

examples.en-GB: The Control Unit sends signals to the ALU, registers, and memory to coordinate each stage of the FDE cycle.

data.targetWord: a small, very fast memory store located inside or near the CPU that holds copies of frequently used instructions and data to reduce the number of slower RAM accesses required

examples.en-GB: The CPU checks the cache first; if the required instruction is there (a cache hit), it is read much faster than fetching from RAM.

data.targetWord: an extremely small, ultra-fast memory location inside the CPU that temporarily holds data or an instruction the processor is actively working with

examples.en-GB: Registers are the fastest form of memory in a computer because they are built directly into the CPU chip.

data.targetWord: a register inside the CPU that holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched from RAM; it is incremented after each fetch

examples.en-GB: After the CPU fetches the instruction at address 0042, the Program Counter is incremented to 0043 for the next fetch.

data.targetWord: a register inside the CPU that stores the result of the most recent arithmetic or logical operation performed by the ALU

examples.en-GB: After the ALU adds 5 to 10, the result (15) is stored in the Accumulator ready for the next operation.

data.targetWord: the first stage of the FDE cycle in which the CPU reads the address in the Program Counter and retrieves the instruction stored at that address in RAM

examples.en-GB: During the fetch stage, the Control Unit retrieves the next instruction from the memory address stored in the Program Counter.

data.targetWord: the second stage of the FDE cycle in which the Control Unit interprets the fetched instruction to determine what operation is required and what data is needed

examples.en-GB: During the decode stage, the Control Unit reads the instruction and identifies it as an addition operation needing two operands.

data.targetWord: the third stage of the FDE cycle in which the relevant CPU component carries out the decoded instruction, for example the ALU performing a calculation

examples.en-GB: During the execute stage, the ALU performs the addition and stores the result in the Accumulator.

data.targetWord: the Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle; the continuous three-stage process by which a CPU processes every instruction in a program, repeated billions of times per second

examples.en-GB: Every instruction in every program running on a computer goes through the FDE cycle: fetch, decode, then execute.

data.targetWord: the number of processing cycles a CPU performs per second, measured in GHz; a higher clock speed means more instructions can be processed per second

examples.en-GB: Upgrading to a CPU with a higher clock speed means the FDE cycle repeats more times every second, so programs run faster.

data.targetWord: gigahertz; the unit used to measure CPU clock speed; one GHz equals one billion cycles per second

examples.en-GB: A CPU running at 3.2 GHz completes 3,200,000,000 clock cycles every second.

data.targetWord: a complete, independent processing unit within a CPU; each core can fetch, decode, and execute instructions simultaneously, allowing true parallel processing

examples.en-GB: A quad-core CPU has four independent cores, each running its own FDE cycle simultaneously.

data.targetWord: a CPU that contains two or more independent processing cores on a single chip, allowing genuinely parallel execution of multiple tasks

examples.en-GB: The multi-core processor allows the laptop to run a video, a browser, and a background update all at the same time without slowing down.

data.targetWord: the design principle underlying modern computers in which program instructions and data are stored together in the same RAM using the same binary format

examples.en-GB: Because of Von Neumann architecture, the same RAM stores both the word processor program and the document you are writing.

data.targetWord: the concept that both a program's instructions and its data are stored in the same memory (RAM) and fetched by the CPU as needed

examples.en-GB: The stored program concept means the CPU can run any program by fetching instructions from RAM, rather than having fixed wired-in logic.

data.targetWord: a single command in a program that the CPU can fetch, decode, and execute; instructions specify operations such as add, move, or jump

examples.en-GB: An instruction such as ADD 5 tells the CPU to add the value 5 to whatever is currently in the Accumulator.

data.targetWord: Random Access Memory; the main volatile memory that stores the instructions and data of currently running programs, accessed by the CPU during the FDE cycle

examples.en-GB: During the fetch stage, the CPU retrieves the next instruction from the location in RAM pointed to by the Program Counter.

data.targetWord: an electrical pathway on the motherboard that carries data, addresses, or control signals between the CPU and other components such as RAM

examples.en-GB: The address bus carries the memory address from the CPU to RAM during the fetch stage so the correct instruction can be retrieved.

data.targetWord: a bus that carries actual data values between the CPU and RAM or other components during the fetch and execute stages

examples.en-GB: The fetched instruction travels from RAM to the CPU along the data bus.

data.targetWord: a bus that carries memory addresses from the CPU to RAM, specifying which location in RAM should be read from or written to

examples.en-GB: The CPU sends the address stored in the Program Counter to RAM via the address bus during the fetch stage.

data.targetWord: a bus that carries control signals from the Control Unit to coordinate the activities of other components, such as telling RAM whether it should perform a read or write operation

examples.en-GB: The control bus sends a read signal to RAM during the fetch stage, instructing it to output the data at the requested address.

data.targetWord: a technique where the CPU begins fetching the next instruction before the previous one has finished executing, overlapping stages to improve throughput

examples.en-GB: Pipelining allows the CPU to fetch instruction 2 while decoding instruction 1, increasing the number of instructions completed per second.

data.targetWord: a single tick of the CPU's clock; the basic unit of time for CPU operations; one clock cycle is the time between two pulses of the clock signal

examples.en-GB: A CPU running at 1 GHz completes one billion clock cycles per second, with some instructions taking multiple cycles.

data.targetWord: the complete set of binary instructions that a particular CPU is designed to understand and execute

examples.en-GB: Different processor families have different instruction sets, which is why programs compiled for one CPU may not run on another.

data.targetWord: the number of instructions a CPU completes per second; increased by higher clock speed, more cores, and better use of cache

examples.en-GB: Adding more cores to a CPU increases throughput for multi-threaded tasks by allowing parallel instruction execution.

data.targetWord: the delay between a request for data and the data becoming available; cache has very low latency compared to RAM, and RAM has lower latency than secondary storage

examples.en-GB: Storing frequently used data in cache reduces latency because the CPU does not have to wait for a slower RAM access.

data.sentence: The ALU performs all ____ and logical operations inside the CPU.
The ____ Unit coordinates the FDE cycle and directs the flow of data between the CPU's components and RAM.
Cache is located inside or near the CPU and is ____ than RAM, allowing faster access to frequently used instructions.
The Program Counter holds the ____ address of the next instruction to be fetched from RAM.
During the ____ stage of the FDE cycle, the CPU retrieves an instruction from the memory address held in the Program Counter.
During the ____ stage, the Control Unit interprets the fetched instruction and works out what operation needs to be carried out.
During the ____ stage, the relevant component (e.g. the ALU) carries out the operation specified by the instruction.
After the fetch stage, the Program Counter is ____ so that it points to the address of the next instruction.
CPU clock speed is measured in ____, which stands for gigahertz — billions of cycles per second.
A CPU with more ____ can execute multiple tasks truly simultaneously, one task per core.
A larger ____ reduces the number of times the CPU must access the slower RAM, improving overall performance.
The Accumulator stores the ____ of the most recent ALU operation.
Von Neumann architecture stores both program ____ and data in the same RAM.
When the CPU finds required data in the cache, this is called a cache ____; when it is not there, the CPU must fetch it from RAM.
The three stages of the FDE cycle in the correct order are: fetch, ____, execute.
More cores improve performance for tasks that can run in ____; a single-threaded program that cannot be parallelised only uses one core.
The ____ bus carries the memory address from the CPU to RAM to specify which instruction to retrieve.
The Control Unit does ____ perform calculations; that is the role of the ALU.
Higher clock speed means the FDE cycle repeats more times per second, so more ____ are processed per second.
Registers are the ____ type of memory in a computer because they are built directly into the CPU.
Higher clock speed generates more ____, which limits how fast a CPU can be clocked before it overheats.
The ____ performs logical comparisons such as AND, OR, and NOT inside the CPU.

data.title: The Three Stages of the FDE Cycle
data.instruction: Place the three stages of the Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle in the correct order.
items: Fetch: the Control Unit reads the Program Counter and retrieves the instruction from that address in RAM; the Program Counter is incremented
Decode: the Control Unit interprets the fetched instruction and determines what operation is required and what data is needed
Execute: the relevant component (e.g. the ALU) carries out the operation; the result may be stored in a register or written back to RAM

data.title: Detailed Steps of the Fetch Stage
data.instruction: Put these steps of the Fetch stage in the correct order.
items: The Control Unit reads the address stored in the Program Counter (PC)
The address is sent to RAM via the address bus
RAM outputs the instruction stored at that address via the data bus
The instruction is copied into a register inside the CPU
The Program Counter is incremented to point to the next instruction's address
